verdict.rationale: Hoppscotch's CLI can run API tests/monitoring from a terminal or automated system (e.g., CI/cron), and its MCP server lets an AI agent read/modify collections and fire real HTTP requests, both of which support background automation. However, these require an external scheduler/host agent to trigger runs — there's no evidence of a built-in autonomous scheduler or persistent background job runner within Hoppscotch itself. Missing for 10: native scheduled/triggered automation, evidence of fully unattended multi-step agent loops, and independent confirmation of autonomous background execution.
